text: {lead} nudges the loose stones back into the gap in the drystone wall, one at a time, and the sheep, who had been about to leave, change their minds. The shepherd leaves a flask of tea on the post.
Something glints in a lochan. {lead} wades in, makes a few calm passes and fishes it out: a walker's purse, a bit damp.
{lead} leans into the leaning trunk and it comes down with a thump, right across the burn, which makes a bridge. On the far side, a few coins in a tin.
{lead} nudges the loose stones of the drystone wall back into line, one at a time. The farmer leaves a flask of tea on the post.
Something glints in the shallows. {lead} wades in, makes a few calm passes and fishes it out: a tin of toffee, a bit damp.
Something glints in the surf. {lead} wades in, makes a few calm passes and fishes it out: a purse, a bit salty.
Sheep at the gate, and no sheep will go first. {lead} comes round the back, low and quiet, and the flock files through. The crofter's thanks: a pasty.
A fresh molehill, and a hopeful hum. {lead} wriggles on the spot and up come the worms, in their dozens, to a crofter's applause: a few coins in the grass.
Something glints in the harbour water. {lead} wades in, makes a few calm passes and fishes it out: a purse, a bit damp.
{lead} takes a run up and lofts the bowl clean over the verge. Where it comes down: a farmer's tip.
